english.title: Adapt / maintain / repair a gaming machine not in accordance with operating licence / exception - Gambling Act 2005
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..)

(A)_[adapted]_
(B)_[maintained]_
(C)_[repaired]_

(D)_[a gaming machine,]_
(E)_[part of a gaming machine,]_

namely **(..SPECIFY GAMING MACHINE..), other than in accordance with an operating licence issued under section 65(1) of the Gambling Act 2005 or an exception under that Act
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 243(1) and 246(1) of the Gambling Act 2005.

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure

english.notes:
(i) Section 243(1)(b) of the Gambling Act 2005 provides exceptions to the offence if the person makes the gaming machine available for use by an individual, and the individual does not, by using the machine, acquire an opportunity to win a prize, section 248 of the Gambling Act 2005, and if the person maintains/repairs the gaming machine in accordance with a single-machine supply and maintenance permit under section 250 of the Gambling Act 2005.
(ii) For the territorial application of this section see section 251 of the Gambling Act 2005.

other.penalty:
Fifty one weeks imprisonment and/or a fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale.

Time limit for prosecutions:
12 months

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
